items.title: A Small Genuine Benefit: Eating Not to Survive, but to practise

items.zh: 又此段食有少勝利。此復云何？謂即此身由食而住，依食而立，非無有食。云何名為有少勝利？謂即如是依食住身，最極久住或經百年。若正將養，或過少分，或有未滿而便夭沒。若唯修此身暫住行，非為妙行；若於如是身暫時住而生喜足，非妙喜足。亦非領受飲食所作圓滿無罪功德勝利。若不唯修身暫住行，亦不唯於身暫時住而生喜足，而即依此暫時住身，修集梵行令得圓滿，乃為妙行，亦妙喜足。又能領受飲食所作圓滿無罪功德勝利。
items.en: This solid food, further, has a small genuine benefit. …It is that this very body abides through food, is established through food, and cannot exist without food. …If one only sustains the body's temporary existence, this is not excellent conduct; if one merely finds contentment in the body's temporary existence, this is not excellent contentment, nor the full, blameless benefit that receiving food can accomplish. If one does not merely sustain the body's temporary existence, nor merely find contentment in it, but instead, resting on this temporarily sustained body, brings pure conduct to fulfilment — this is excellent conduct, and excellent contentment. It also achieves the full, blameless benefit that receiving food can accomplish.

items.zh: 應自思惟：我若與彼愚夫同分，修諸愚夫同分之行，非我所宜；我若於此下劣段食少分勝利安住喜足，亦非我宜。

items.title: Eating Like It Were Your Own Child's Flesh: Gratitude, Purity, and Freedom From Resentment

items.zh: 若於如是遍一切種段食過患圓滿知已，以正思擇，深見過患，而求出離。為求如是食出離故，如子肉想，食於段食。應作是念：彼諸施主，甚大艱難積集財寶，具受廣大追求所作種種過患。由悲愍故，求勝果故，如割皮肉及以刺血，而相惠施。我得此食，宜應如是方便受用。謂應如法而自安處，無倒受用，報施主恩，令獲最勝大果、大利、大榮、大盛。當隨月喻往施主家，盪滌身心，安住慚愧。遠離憍傲，不自高舉，不輕蔑他。如自獲得所有利養，心生喜悅，如是於他所得利養，心亦喜悅。又應如是自持其心往施主家。豈有出家往詣他所，要望他施非不惠施，要望他敬非不恭敬，要多非少，要妙非麁，要當速疾而非遲緩。
items.en: Having fully understood every kind of fault inherent in solid food, one, through correct discernment, sees these faults deeply and seeks to be free of them. In order to seek this freedom, one eats solid food as though it were the flesh of one's own child. One should reflect: those benefactors, with the greatest difficulty, accumulated this wealth, undergoing every manner of fault in its pursuit. Out of compassion, and seeking an excellent result, they give it as though cutting their own flesh and drawing their own blood. …One should approach a benefactor's home like the moon [clear and cool, free of burning heat] — cleansing body and mind, abiding in a sense of shame and conscience, free of arrogance, neither exalting oneself nor disdaining others. Just as one feels joy upon receiving support oneself, so too should one feel joy when another receives it. …How could one who has gone forth, visiting another's home, insist that they must give and not withhold, must show respect and not fail to, must give much and not little, must give something fine and not something coarse, must give quickly and not slowly?

items.title: Section: Freedom From Resentment Completes, and the Four Kinds of Food That Sustain a Being

items.zh: 應作是心，往施主家：設不惠施，終不於彼起怨害心及瞋恚心而相嫌恨。勿我由此起怨害心及瞋恚心增上緣力，身壞已後生諸惡趣，多受困厄。設不恭敬而非恭敬，設少非多，設麁非妙，設復遲緩而非速疾，亦不於彼起怨害心及瞋恚心而相嫌恨。如前廣說。又我應依所食段食，發起如是如是正行，及於其量如實了達。謂我命根由此不滅，又於此食不苦耽著，纔能隨順攝受梵行。如是我今住沙門性、住出家性，受用飲食，如法清淨，遠離眾罪。由是諸相，以正思擇食於所食。云何所食？謂四種食。一者、段食，二者、觸食，三者、意等思食，四者、識食。今此義中意說段食。此復云何？謂餅、麨、飯、羹、臛、糜、粥、酥油、糖、蜜、魚、肉、𦵔鮓、乳、酪、生酥、薑、鹽、酢等種種品類，和雜為摶，段段吞食；故名段食。
items.en: One should approach a benefactor's home with this resolve: even should no gift be given at all, one will never, on that account, give rise to resentment or ill will. …I should, in dependence on this solid food I eat, arouse conduct of exactly this kind, and understand its proper measure exactly as it is — knowing that my life-faculty is sustained by it, yet neither afflicting myself nor clinging to it, so that it may serve only to support pure conduct. …What is eaten? There are four kinds of food: solid food; contact as food; volition and intention as food; and consciousness as food. In the present context, solid food alone is meant. What is this? Cakes, roasted grain flour, rice, soup, meat broth, gruel, ghee, sugar, honey, fish, meat, pickled preserves, milk, yogurt, fresh cream, ginger, salt, vinegar, and various other kinds, mixed together into a mouthful and swallowed piece by piece — this is why it is called solid food.

items.zh: 所言食者，所謂飡、噉、咀嚼、吞咽、甞、啜、飲等名之差別。

items.title: Not Eating to Fuel Indulgence: The First of Four Wrong Motives

items.zh: 云何名為不為倡蕩？謂如有一樂受欲者，為受諸欲食於所食。彼作是思：我食所食，令身飽滿、令身充悅。過日晚時至於夜分，當與姝妙嚴飾女人共為嬉戲，歡娛受樂，倡掉縱逸。
items.en: What is called not eating for the sake of wanton pleasure? It is like one who delights in sensual pleasure, eating for the sake of experiencing those pleasures. Such a person thinks: "I eat this food so that my body will be full and content. When the day passes into evening and night falls, I shall enjoy myself with beautifully adorned women, delighting in pleasure, indulgent and unrestrained." …Wanton pleasure means that, within this noble Dharma and discipline, one who indulges desire is driven by craving and lust into every kind of unwholesome, improper thought; eating for this reason leaves all the faculties agitated, the mind restless, uneasy, and never at peace. Eating for this purpose is called eating for the sake of wanton pleasure. …The many learned noble disciples, however, through the power of discernment, see these faults deeply, know well how to be free of them, and eat accordingly — not as those driven by desire eat. This is why it is called not eating for the sake of wanton pleasure.

items.zh: 言倡蕩者，於此聖法毘奈耶中，說受欲者欲貪所引、婬逸所引所有諸惡不善尋思。由此食噉所食噉時，令其諸根皆悉掉舉，令意躁擾、令意不安、令意不靜。若為此事食所食者，名為倡蕩食於所食。諸有多聞聖弟子眾，以思擇力，深見過患，善知出離、而食所食；非如前說諸受欲者食於所食；是故名為不為倡蕩。云何名為不為憍逸、不為飾好、不為端嚴？

blocks.text: After the faults, the one real benefit, and the right attitude in eating. The image of "a child's flesh" comes from a well-known sūtra parable. One passage (0409b27) is untranslated.
"This very body abides through food, and cannot exist without food." Simply sustaining the body is not excellent conduct; using the sustained body to fulfil the holy life is.

subs.head: As if it were a child's flesh

blocks.text: "One eats solid food as though it were the flesh of one's own child." In the parable, parents crossing a desert with nothing left to eat must eat their child's flesh to survive, and they eat without any relish. Master Cháng Bǎi: for monastics, the donors give "as though cutting their own flesh"; one must repay that kindness. Before attaining the path, one is only a nominal member of the Saṅgha jewel, and should not be proud.
"Just as one feels joy upon receiving support oneself, so should one feel joy when another receives it." Venerable Miào Jìng: don't think, "This supporter gave more to him than to me."

subs.head: Freedom from resentment; four kinds of food

blocks.text: "Even should no gift be given at all, one will never give rise to resentment." There are four kinds of food: solid food, contact, volition, and consciousness; here only solid food is meant. Venerable Miào Jìng: the life faculty is what keeps body and mind together; food keeps it from ceasing. Master Cháng Bǎi: one resolved to learn the Dharma "keeps living"; hope itself sustains.

The first wrong motive: eating to fuel sensual pleasure. The untranslated prose (0409b27) explains: such eating makes the senses restless and the mind agitated; the learned noble disciple eats with discernment, seeing its dangers. Master Cháng Bǎi: the purpose of eating is not to enjoy desire but to become free of it.

quiz.q: What is the "small genuine benefit" of solid food?
options: this body abides through food, is established through food, and cannot exist without it
quiz.why: "It is that this very body abides through food, is established through food, and cannot exist without food." Master Cháng Bǎi: once eaten, food becomes nourishment, blood, skin, and flesh, building the body's tissues — that is "established through food."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is it if one only sustains the body's temporary existence?
options: not excellent conduct; and contentment in it is not excellent contentment
quiz.why: "If one only sustains the body's temporary existence, this is not excellent conduct; if one merely finds contentment in the body's temporary existence, this is not excellent contentment." Venerable Miào Jìng: it is not counted a good thing — though not a bad one either.

quiz.q: To seek freedom from food, how does the treatise say one should eat solid food?
options: as medicine, the more the better
as though it were the flesh of one's own child
as poison, not eating at all
quiz.why: "In order to seek this freedom, one eats solid food as though it were the flesh of one's own child." Venerable Miào Jìng: when eating, think of it as eating one's own son's flesh.

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what does the child's-flesh image remind the practitioner to do?
options: to repay kindness — the donors are as if cutting their own flesh to support monastics
quiz.why: The donors give as though cutting their own flesh and drawing their own blood. Master Cháng Bǎi: the story reminds practitioners to repay kindness, for the donors are as if cutting their own flesh to support monastics' practice.

quiz.q: When another receives support, how does the treatise say one should feel?
options: joyful, just as when one receives it oneself
quiz.why: "Just as one feels joy upon receiving support oneself, so too should one feel joy when another receives it." Venerable Miào Jìng: don't say, "This lay supporter is mine — you can't beg here."

quiz.q: If a donor gives nothing, how does the treatise say one should respond?
options: never give rise to resentment or ill will towards them
quiz.why: "Even should no gift be given at all, one will never, on that account, give rise to resentment or ill will." Master Cháng Bǎi: be glad whatever is given, and glad if nothing is; resentment sows the cause of falling into the lower realms.

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of food, and which is meant here?
options: vegetarian, meat, sweet, salty; vegetarian is meant
solid food, contact, volition, and consciousness; solid food is meant
breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper; lunch is meant
food of gods, humans, ghosts, animals; human food is meant
quiz.why: "There are four kinds of food: solid food; contact as food; volition and intention as food; and consciousness as food. In the present context, solid food alone is meant." Master Cháng Bǎi: consciousness as food is marked by holding — the storehouse consciousness, nourished by the other three, keeps holding the body.
